verified.entry_point: A network client holding the API token drives the running test-runner control server over its WebSocket RPC (UI API) and over the browser-mode file command functions and the HTTP test-evidence endpoints those servers expose. Reproduced on the pinned+injected tree: a client connected to the live server (createVitest with api host 0.0.0.0, watch:true, token from config) overwrites a registered test file and starts runs; the browser file commands, called with the browser project the runner resolves for a 0.0.0.0 api/browser.api host, create/remove files and export artifacts; the HTTP evidence endpoints write a file and return a file outside the project under widened file-serving settings.
sites: packages/vitest/src/api/setup.ts saveTestFile (write), rerun/rerunTask (exec), updateSnapshot (exec+write) — reported site, published fix

packages/vitest/src/node/config/resolveConfig.ts resolveApiServerConfig — producer: localhost/unset/port-number -> local, network host -> exposed, browser.api unset vs set (enforced by input-shape variants inside the A1/A2/S* tests)
packages/browser/src/node/plugin.ts GET /__vitest_attachment__ — uncovered route: read accepts any path when server.fs.strict is false

packages/browser/src/node/commands/fs.ts writeFile path escape under widened serving — uncovered write form of the same confinement hole (both Vite serving helpers return true when server.fs.strict is false)
routes_investigated_not_built: UI source-viewer read handlers (getExternalResult/getTransformResult) use the deprecated serving check: in vite 7.1.5 the stricter loading check ALSO returns true when server.fs.strict=false, so the published fix's read-path change is a no-op and the bypass is not fix-closable there; read-only. Dismissed as a standalone lever; the confinement invariant is enforced at the attachment read and the write commands instead.

browser-mode RPC write handlers (saveSnapshotFile/removeSnapshotFile/onTaskArtifactRecord): covered by the published fix; driving them deterministically needs a live Playwright browser provider (not offline/deterministic). Out of scope.
injected_siblings: S1: packages/browser/src/node/commands/artifacts.ts exportArtifact (+ registration in commands/index.ts) — extra browser command that writes a test-evidence artifact, copying the pre-fix writeFile shape exactly (resolve under root, file check, mkdir, write). Published fix never touches artifacts.ts or commands/index.ts.

S2: packages/ui/node/index.ts POST /__vitest_attachment__ — HTTP write companion on the UI's attachment read-back path; a maintainer adding 'save an attachment' adds the matching POST to the same middleware. Published fix never touches packages/ui/node.
verified.project_tests_run: The runner's own offline config-resolution behaviour (api flag resolution, localhost vs network defaults, browser.api inheritance) is reproduced by the functional/security pair via createVitest. Browser-mode and UI Playwright e2e specs were deliberately NOT used (GUI/flaky/offline-incompatible). vitest + @vitest/browser + @vitest/ui build and the hidden suites run on node 20 with the repo's own toolchain.
verified.seam_notes: Grading uses a pristine runner copied at image build (/opt/vitest-verifier: cp -a /app/packages + tsconfig.base.json, node_modules linked to /app/node_modules). Tests live under /opt/vitest-verifier/packages/vitest/__verifier__ so vitest/birpc/flatted/ws resolve to the pristine copy; the verifier config aliases vitest/node, @vitest/browser-preview and the browser command sources (@verifier/browser-commands, @verifier/browser-artifacts) to /app. test.sh rebuilds vitest + @vitest/browser + @vitest/ui from the agent's src first. Browser command tests get their project from real config resolution: createVitest with api.host and an inline browser project (preview provider, browser.api.host = same host unless unsetBrowserApi), then _initBrowserServers(); no browser is launched. Widened serving is a normal config file with server.fs.strict:false that the browser project extends.

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: a clean thrown client error with no side effect is an acceptable refusal here; the security tests assert the effect (file unchanged, no run started), not silence, so a throwing fix passes
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: each operation acts on the file/task it names; there is no proxy or neighbouring resource to authorise instead of the one touched
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: reads are not an attack vector; the positive-control read tests guard against a fix that instead blocks reads (modelled by reads_blocked.patch)
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the write/exec decision is taken from the server's resolved local-vs-network configuration before any attacker-supplied path is used; there is no normalising step on the input to place the guard after
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the access token is compared with a constant-time equality and the local-vs-network decision reads the configured bind host; there is no attacker-controlled spelling of an identity for a guard to mis-parse
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the authority is the server's own resolved configuration, never an external service that could be absent; an unrecognised host is treated as network-reachable (fail closed)

notes: Pattern A+B: the reported UI write/exec site (A1) plus a far second implementation (A2) and the producer (A3), together with two real uncovered confinement routes (B1 attachment read, B2 write-form path escape) whose hardness comes from vite 7.1.5 returning true from BOTH serving helpers when server.fs.strict is false — the published fix's switch to the newer helper is a no-op for that bypass. Two injected siblings (S1 artifact export, S2 HTTP evidence save) sit where the published fix never looks. The instruction states both invariants (authorization and confinement, the latter with a 'whatever file-serving settings' clause) without naming any site.
